A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiLQ benchmark. Their main text, seven tables, nine figures, and Appendices A and B are readable and support reliable matching across layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original query-quality and preference evaluations, retrieval experiments, annotator interviews, and token-level and part-of-speech analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and 6–7 and the analyses in Figures 2–3 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The query-construction procedure, three ColBERT distillation variants, and Translate-Test procedure remain unchanged. Added implementation names and resource citations document existing components without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MSMARCO training source, CLEF00–03 and NeuCLIR22 collections, English plus eight other languages, and MonoIR, CLIR, and MQIR scenarios. Table 5's added EN column clarifies the English corpus already described in v1.

E2.justification: Figure 2 and Tables 6–7 retain BM25, mContriever, and Mono-, Mixed-, and Cross-Distill. Table 3 retains the same translation-assisted comparisons. Newly identifying Pyserini and the mContriever checkpoint does not establish a changed comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1, Table 5 revises the reported CLEF passage count from 1.02M to 1.01M. This is a limited revision to the stated evaluation collection size; the PDFs do not establish that preprocessing or experiments were rerun. Query counts, metrics, passage-length limits, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Translate-Test analysis, token-level case study, annotator interviews, and part-of-speech analysis are retained. The new ANN-indexing variability remark in Appendix B.3 supplies no documented sensitivity experiment or supporting analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly discloses that all experiments used a single run and discusses possible ANN-indexing variability. V1 gives no run count. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or quantified variability estimates are added; this disclosure does not establish a change in runs performed.

E6.justification: The numerical annotation and retrieval results remain unchanged, including all 186 numerical entries in Tables 6–7 and the plotted results. V2 adds one unquantified qualitative observation in Appendix B.3: ANN-indexing variations reportedly do not cause substantial result differences.

T1.justification: The Code-Mixing Index definition in Appendix A.3, Equation 1, and the underlying conceptual assumptions are unchanged. Neither version adds mathematical propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same benchmark, evaluation, and English-mixing contributions. The abstract and introduction replace 'highly preferred' with 'relatively preferred,' but the substantive preference comparison is unchanged and the conclusion still asserts high user preference. This is wording calibration rather than a redefined contribution.

C2.justification: The expanded Ethical Considerations explicitly limits generalization beyond the news domain and nine evaluated languages, discusses possible bias toward high-resource languages, and qualifies commercial applicability. Existing Section 6 limitations and the main explanations of retrieval behavior are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds code and MiLQ catalogue access instructions, dataset licensing information, and explicit Pyserini/Lucene and facebook/mcontriever-msmarco implementation identifiers. It revises the stated NeuCLIR license and discloses separate validation annotators and informed consent. Existing hardware, optimization settings, and annotation payment details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds resource citations including PanLex, Conneau et al.'s word-translation work, and Pyserini. These improve attribution for existing components; positioning as the first public user-crafted MQIR benchmark and the broader relationship to prior research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the conclusion, expands Ethical Considerations into labeled subsections, adds acknowledgments, and updates an author's affiliation and contact information. Preference wording is softened, while the main section sequence and scientific narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 5 adds an EN column and places the shared English corpus statistics there. Figure 3's caption changes Cross-R to Cross-Distill. Tables and figures undergo limited resizing, spacing, and relocation, while their underlying visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency and usability through explicit code/data access and licensing information, clearer baseline implementation details, single-run disclosure, and more specific applicability limitations. These are useful refinements to an otherwise unchanged empirical study. The added ANN-stability assertion remains unquantified, so it provides little additional evidential strength.
